content.introduction: UK inflation rate was 3.3% in March 2026, up from 3% in February, driven by global energy costs. The Bank of England kept interest rates at 3.75%, anticipating further inflation hikes if oil prices remain high.
body: # Why are UK prices rising more quickly? **Prices in the UK rose by 3.3% in the year to March, up from the 3% recorded in January and February, and above the Bank of England's 2% target.**. These were the first official inflation figures since the start of the US-Israel war with Iran, which has put up energy and fuel costs around the world. The Bank moves interest rates up and down to try to keep inflation on track. Six cuts since August 2024 had brought rates down to 3.75%, but the war is expected to delay any further falls, and the next move could be up. ## What is inflation? Inflation is the increase in the price of something over time. ## How is the UK's inflation rate measured? ## What is happening to UK inflation? Core CPI was 3.1% in the 12 months to March, down from 3.2% in February.

Although [the March CPI figure of 3.3%](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cnv8l17r51ro)remains above the Bank of England's target, it is well below the 11.1% figure reached in October 2022. ## [Three ways the latest inflation figures affect you](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c75k002qkzno). The vote was equally close in February, when policymakers decided to [keep rates at 3.75%](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/czx1vly05pvo). At its March meeting the Bank's monetary policy committee [voted unanimously to keep rates at 3.75%](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c8d5dee3ep8o), in anticipation of higher inflation. At its April meeting, [the Bank again held rates at 3.75%](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cg7p89mp2rjo), but warned that future hikes were likely if the price of oil remained high, pushing UK inflation up. ## [Will UK interest rates go up?](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c3dky111m40o). The [unemployment rate was 4.9% in the three months to February](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cjd84pkkjgpo), down from 5.2% in the previous quarter. In March and [again in April](https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c62rm4zk3kgo), the US Federal Reserve held its target interest rate at a range of 3.50% to 3.75% — the lowest level in three years.
